page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, alongside poor single-threaded gzip compression speeds in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core performance is average, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached reads and writes also registers in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.8xlarge offers a high-density memory configuration relative to its processing cores, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution for multi-threaded tasks. Appropriate workloads include database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference, where multi-core execution and memory capacity are prioritized over raw single-core speed.
